findings.title: Client upload validation ignores site size settings
findings.body: validateUploadedFile now uses a hard-coded 10 MB maximum for both image and attachment types instead of Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']. The 413 handler in displayErrorForUpload (line 246) uses the same hard-coded value. Attachments are not downsized server-side, so this allows users to select and submit files beyond max_attachment_size_kb and gives users an incorrect maximum, while also blocking sites that allow uploads larger than 10 MB.

findings.title: API URL download cap ignores type-specific size settings
findings.body: FileHelper.download is now always capped at 10.megabytes instead of the configured upload size. The new downsize path only applies to images and only when max_image_size_kb > 0, so non-image API uploads can still be downloaded and processed far above max_attachment_size_kb, and image uploads can be accepted beyond the intended limit if downsize fails. Use the type-specific site setting or enforce the limit after download.

findings.title: Loop uses stale Tempfile#size after in-place resize
findings.body: tempfile is normally a Tempfile (Rack uploaded files and FileHelper.download). Tempfile#size caches the file size, so after OptimizedImage.downsize rewrites the same file outside the Tempfile object, tempfile.size at line 66 still returns the original size. The loop can run all five 80% reductions even after the image is below max_image_size_kb, degrading the image, and Upload.create_for is called with the stale original size at line 72. Use File.size(tempfile.path) after each downsize or otherwise refresh/reopen the file.

findings.title: No final size check after downsize loop
findings.body: The return value of OptimizedImage.downsize is ignored and there is no check after the loop that the resulting file is at or below SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes. If the ImageMagick/gifsicle command fails, or if five 80% reductions are not enough for a very large file, the code still calls Upload.create_for with an oversized image. This silently bypasses the configured max image size. Check the result and return an upload error if the image cannot be reduced below the limit.

findings.title: Duplicate self.downsize overrides the legacy width/height form
findings.body: Ruby does not support method overloading; this second definition of self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={}) replaces the first definition at line 145 (from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={}). Any caller using the existing numeric width/height form now gets an ArgumentError, and the first method is dead code. Either keep only the new method and update callers, or replace both with a single method that accepts both forms.

findings.title: Animated GIF uploads via API are flattened
findings.body: OptimizedImage.optimize chooses the animated gifsicle path by testing the source path for a .GIF extension (optimized_image.rb line 155). Here the source is tempfile.path, but FileHelper.download creates a Tempfile named discourse-upload-<type> without the original extension. An animated GIF fetched from an API URL will therefore go through the ImageMagick non-animated path (from[0]) and be reduced to its first frame, losing animation even though allow_animation is passed. Detect animation from the original filename/content type rather than the temporary path.
